title: Incumbent algorithm gives inconsistent results for timer callbacks and event handlers; remove skip-when-determining-incumbent counter?
body:
Working on <https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=163412> led me to implement the incumbent concept in WebKit. As pointed out by Geoffrey Garen in his review of the patch in <https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=163412#c44>, the [current algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#incumbent) to determine the incumbent setting/realm/global object returns inconsistent results depending on how it was invoked.  In particular, the existence of the skip\-when\-determining\-incumbent counter flag means that "Not all entry-points [to the algorithm] agree on whether they override the incumbent global object on the JavaScript stack or not. For example, mutation event listeners do override, but timers don't. That behavior is surprising and bad." This discrepancy is illustrated with the following example:

Create two pages A.html and B.html with the respective markup below:

In A.html:
```
<script>
window.name = "A";

function sendMessageFromAToB()
{
    window.B.postMessage("hello from A", "*");
}
</script>
<iframe src="B.html"></iframe>
```

In B.html:
```
<script>
window.name = "B";

window.top.document.body.addEventListener("dummy", window.top.sendMessageFromAToB, false); // (1)

window.top.document.body.dispatchEvent(new Event("dummy")); // (2)

window.onmessage = function (messageEvent)
{
    alert(`Got message from ${messageEvent.source.name}: '${messageEvent.data}'`);
}
</script>
```

Access A.html over HTTP in a browser. According to the incumbent algorithm, you should see a JavaScript alert with message "Got message from B: 'hello from A'" because the skip-when-determining-incumbent counter > 0 (by (2) and [**prepare to run a callback** algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#prepare-to-run-a-callback)) and B's global object is at the top of the backup incumbent stack as it was saved in (1) (see  remark (*)). We would have expected to see "Got message from A: 'hello from A'" and this is consistent with the behavior observed in Safari for Mac 10.1 (12603.1.24), Firefox for Mac 53.0.3 (64-bit), Chrome for Mac 59.0.3071.71 (Official Build) beta (64-bit) and Edge 38.14393.1066.0 (EdgeHTML 14.14393). Can we remove skip\-when\-determining\-incumbent counter flag?

(*) As far as I can tell the standard does not explicitly mention that the incumbent settings/global object is saved when registering an event listener. In section [Event Handler](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-handler-attributes:the-event-handler-processing-algorithm) it quotes non-existent text from the DOM spec (last updated 9 May 2017):

> The EventListener's callback context can be arbitrary; it does not impact the steps of the event handler processing algorithm\. \[DOM\]

However it is mentioned in the ["convoluted example"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#incumbent:skip-when-determining-incumbent-counter-6), bolded text for emphasis:

> a\.html's environment settings object \(**stored as the EventHandler's callback context**\)

And implied by the note in section [Interface types in the WebIDL spec. (Editor's Draft, 18 May 2017)](https://heycam.github.io/webidl/#idl-interface), reproduced here:

> Note: For ECMAScript objects, the callback context is used to hold a reference to the incumbent settings object at the time the Object value is converted to an IDL callback interface type value. See §3.2.13 Interface types.
